text:
maria: Heads-up — getting intermittent TLS cert mismatch errors for a subset of users hitting eu-west-1 via the ALB. Error shows the wildcard cert for *.internal instead of our customer SAN cert. Seen across two services behind the same listener.

jay: Any reproducible steps or client examples?

maria: Repro on my machine with curl and openssl. Example: 
```
openssl s_client -connect foo.prod.redwood.com:443 -servername foo.prod.redwood.com -alpn h2
```
Sometimes returns our prod cert, sometimes returns `*.internal.redwood` (wrong). Happens ~1/20 tries.

oliver: That smells like a partial cert rollout on the ALB nodes. ALB stores certs per node and new certs can take time to propagate. Did we rotate recently?

maria: We rolled the SAN cert last night (auto deploy). No obvious errors in deploy logs.

infra-bot: ALB access log excerpt (sample): 
```
https 2026-03-...? client-ip request-time elb-status-code target-status-code "GET /" "TLS_HANDSHAKE" cert_selector=default
```
(we've got entries where cert_selector=default)

kevin: I ran tcpdump on an nginx-ingress pod and captured the ClientHello. On the failing connections the ClientHello looks identical — SNI present and correct. So client side isn't stripping SNI.

jay: Can we prove which ALB node is returning the wrong cert? Any per-node logs?

oliver: I asked AWS support — ALB does SNI selection per connection. If a node hasn't loaded the new certificate bundle, that node will present the default certificate. That matches the intermittent behavior (requests land on different nodes).

maria: Okay — so rollout consistency issue. Is this the ACM -> ALB attach step that our infra automation does?

kevin: Yes. Our deploy script calls AWS to attach the new ACM cert to the listener. Looks like some ALB nodes accepted earlier than others. AWS says propagation happens asynchronously across the fleet.

sre-oncall: Mitigation plan: 1) re-attach the new cert to force propagation; 2) remove the old wildcard cert from the listener so nodes that don't have the new cert will fail instead of serving the wrong wildcard (safer for detecting failures). Also add an access-log monitor for cert_selector != expected.

maria: Can we reproduce in staging quickly? I can run a looped openssl test against a staging ALB where I add a new cert and watch behaviour.

kevin: I reproduced in staging by attaching a second cert and watching nodes flip. Confirmed intermittent default cert until I forced a listener update (modified listener to reapply certs). After the reapply everything returned sane.

oliver: Long term: update deploy automation to 1) wait for attach confirmation across all ALB nodes (poll API /describe-listener-certificates if available), 2) run a quick probe from multiple AZs that verifies SNI+cert chain for each hostname, 3) do a rolling remove of the old cert only after all probes pass.

jay: Also add an alert: when access logs show >0.1% cert_selector=default for prod hostnames over 5m, page infra-sre.

infra-bot: Created ticket INFRA-4521: "ALB cert propagation validation + probe" assigned to kevin.

maria: For immediate fix I re-applied the listener cert and the number of failures dropped to 0. Reopening if it returns. Thanks all. :tada:

kevin: Follow-up: I added a small smoke test script to the deploy pipeline (runs curl+openssl from 3 AZs). Pushed a PR, will roll out after review.

sre-oncall: Good postmortem notes: root cause=asynchronous ALB node propagation; mitigation=force reapply + staging probes; long-term=deploy gating and monitors.

maria: Filing short runbook in docs (linked to INFRA-4521) on how to reapply listener cert and validate with openssl.

jay: Nice catch. Leaving this thread open for the next 24h to ensure stable.
